newsitem.title: CHINA: Air China cargo handling record detailed.
newsitem.headline: Air China cargo handling record detailed.

text.p: China's national carrier, Air China, flew a total of 10,245 tonnes of cargo to the United States from Beijing in 1996, the magazine Cargonews China said.

Quoting Air China's business division director, Xiaodong Feng, it said 38 percent of export volume from Beijing was destined for Europe in the past calendar year, 24 percent for Japan, 19 percent for Hong Kong and 10 percent to the U.S.. All other export destinations accounted for nine percent of the airline's volume from its Beijing Capital airport base.

Air China's cargo warehouse facilities in Beijing handled more than a quarter of a million tonnes of air cargo in 1996, the magazine said. Internationally generated cargo accounted for 118,675 tonnes but the total has been falling year on year because of a surge in domestic cargo, it added. Domestic cargo handled at the airline's Beijing warehousing facilities totalled 156,778 tonnes in 1996.

Constraints on space at Capital airport may be overcome with the possibility of government approval for a new cargo handling complex on Air China's 20,000 sq m adjacent site by the end of the year, the magazine added.

It said Air China will increase cargo capacity later this year with the scheduled arrival of a Boeing 747 freighter and two B747 Combis along with an Airbus A340. One of its older B747 Combis is also expected to be converted into a freighter.

Quoting sources close to Air China, the magazine said the airline will boast a fleet of almost 70 wide bodied aircraft by the end of this year with plans to add another 20 aircraft by 2000. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
